original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: One measured bottleneck of the selected record's only post-#1042 stage (research/complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges/verify.py -> frozen PR1087 verify_t16.py): the `audit` sub-stage, i.e. the pinned audit_allcold.py (SHA-256 1467a2ac...) with its 15 mutation controls, whose time is dominated by copy.deepcopy. Can an opt-in launcher replace only deepcopy by a checked marshal round trip, leaving every pinned byte, check and control unchanged, with byte-identical outputs on the same fixture?
scope_change_reason: Refined within the card's allowed variation 'Profile one stage': the profiled stage is the selected final stage and the optimized object is one sub-stage's copy primitive. No coverage is removed and no result is cached.
bottleneck_link: Every reviewer of the selected record runs this stage (also with --baseline1042 reuse), and the same audit script runs in the cold baseline1042 `t16` stage and in owner-map candidates built on verify_t16.py. Halving its slowest sub-stage shortens review of complex-side packing/owner candidates without weakening a check.
stop_rule: Stop if any audit output or the merged stage log differs from the in-stage receipt, if the fixture's ASYNC-AUDIT.json differs from the archived selected receipt, or if the speedup required editing pinned code.
evidence: verify.py replays the selected final stage on the archived provider files (audit equals the archived selected ASYNC-AUDIT.json), then reruns the audit sub-stage legacy vs fast in fresh copies: all three written audit files, the written IDLE-REMAINDER-FRAMES.json.gz and the merged stdout/stderr log are byte-identical to the in-stage outputs; 4,838 deepcopy calls all take the marshal path. macOS, 3 alternating rounds: CPython 3.12 legacy 22.37/22.27/22.50 s vs fast 9.05/9.06/9.21 s (2.47x median); CPython 3.14.7 legacy 17.85/18.31/17.79 s vs fast 9.43/9.46/9.47 s (1.89x). Registered replay passes under CPython 3.12. Controls: tampered hosted template rejected by both; unpinned script refused; identity copier detected by byte comparison (the pinned audit itself exits 0 with a corrupted report); fallback semantics for subclass, NaN, custom object, cyclic and memo calls.

open_questions.question: Should the selected replay driver offer an opt-in, source-bound hook that runs the audit sub-stage (and the cold baseline1042 t16 stage) through fast_copy.py?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The launcher is verified here but is not wired into make frontier1094-verify, so reviewers do not yet get the time saving.
open_questions.first_step: Add an opt-in flag to a new driver (not the frozen verify_t16.py) that substitutes the launcher for run_portable.py only for allow-listed script hashes and compares all audit outputs against a legacy run once.
open_questions.blocked_by: A maintainer decision on modifying or wrapping the frozen PR1087 stage runner.

open_questions.question: Which other pinned verifiers spend most of their time in copy.deepcopy of JSON trees for mutation controls (ten distinct audit_allcold.py hashes exist in research/, plus other reject() helpers)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The same checked substitution may speed up historical cold replays and candidate checks with no source edits.
open_questions.first_step: Profile each allow-list candidate on its own committed fixture and extend SCRIPTS only with byte-identical receipts.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each candidate needs its own runnable fixture; many require a long cold upstream replay first.

open_questions.question: What dominates the remaining ~9 s of the audit sub-stage, and can it be reduced without editing the pinned audit?
open_questions.why_it_matters: audit() itself (16 passes over 69,120 helper roles) is now the largest share of the selected final stage.
open_questions.first_step: cProfile the fast path; the per-role list/index scans over 73-column bases are the likely candidates.
open_questions.blocked_by: Further gains likely require an adapter that changes audit() code, which needs a separate equivalence argument.
